name: Citizenship by Naturalisation (Ordinary and Facilitated for Spouses)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires 10 years federal residence (reduced from 12 in 2018), holding a C permit at application, plus additional cantonal and communal residence/integration criteria that vary by jurisdiction.
This requires B1 oral / A2 written in a national language, plus meeting Art. 58a integration criteria (respect for public order, economic/social participation, familiarity with Swiss life).
requirements.fix_path: Take an approved language test at B1 oral / A2 written.

requirement_groups.name: Facilitated naturalisation — spouse resident in Switzerland

requirements.blocker_text: This requires 3 years of marriage to a Swiss citizen and 5 years total Swiss residence (year immediately prior in Switzerland). A C permit is not formally required, though valid residence status must be held throughout. Excluded if the Swiss spouse only naturalised after the marriage.

evidence_required.document: Approved language test at the required level
10 (or 5) years of residence evidence and cantonal/communal integration documentation

notes: GENUINE THREE-LEVEL PROCESS, one of the most administratively complex naturalisation structures in this entire multi-country dataset: federal (SEM naturalisation licence) + cantonal + communal, with cantons and communes free to impose ADDITIONAL residence and integration criteria beyond the federal 10-year minimum — some communes even run local assembly votes on individual applications, a genuinely unique feature not replicated anywhere else in this dataset. SEM federal fee is only CHF 100/150/50 (single/joint/minor) — but cantonal and communal fees add substantially, pushing the REAL total cost to commonly CHF 1,000-3,000+, a stale-figure risk worth flagging since many tier-3 sites quote a single blended 'naturalisation fee' as if it were federal. Facilitated route for spouses: 3 years marriage + 5 years total residence (year immediately prior in Switzerland) — genuinely does NOT require holding a C permit first, unlike the ordinary route, though valid residence status throughout is still required; explicitly EXCLUDED if the Swiss spouse only naturalised themselves after the marriage — a real anti-circumvention rule worth flagging. Dual citizenship confirmed permitted for both routes.
